# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments (fictional)

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel (Sponsor)
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, twelve weeks, US$60,000
**Source:** Client Profile Block v1.0, drawing on discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands, operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, and has about 1,100 staff. The Client describes its AI maturity as piloting. It has stated three AI use cases:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

Several drivers make governance timely:

- **Internal audit finding.** A June 2026 internal audit finding recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems.
- **Regulation.** The stated regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj) and GDPR (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj).
- **Certification work.** ISO/IEC 42001 (https://www.iso.org/standard/81230.html) is a certification target, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed.
- **Sponsor objective.** Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The Client has also stated three constraints:

1. Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
2. Customer data must stay in the EU.
3. The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

The Client lists two incumbent frameworks: an ISO/IEC 27001 (https://www.iso.org/standard/27001) information security management system and an ISO 9001 (https://www.iso.org/standard/62085.html) quality management system. These names tell us which management system disciplines exist. They do not tell us which registers, processes, controls or records the Client holds. Integration points with them are therefore marked `Unknown` below until the attaching artifacts are identified at Week 1.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A conventional consulting engagement would leave the Client with a set of documents produced by outsiders. The Guided AI GRC Build reverses that model. The Client's own build team does the work in weekly workshops, coaching sessions and structured asynchronous implementation. As a result, the people who will operate the system after Week 12 are the people who built it.

This approach suits Tamarack for three reasons:

1. **The finding needs an owned process.** The internal audit finding concerns an inventory. Inventories decay unless the people who maintain them understand why each entry exists.
2. **The Q2 2027 objective needs operating governance.** Your objective concerns a production deployment, so governance has to be operating rather than documented on paper.
3. **The team already knows management system work.** The roles in the build team already work within, or alongside, ISO management system disciplines. A guided build lets that experience carry over into the AI Management System (AIMS) instead of creating a parallel structure.

**Frameworks.** The program uses two frameworks:

- the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) for the governance, risk and compliance spine
- the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) for governed workflows and human oversight

Steering materials draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) as the board-layer reference.

**Principles.** The program is guided by three principles: Slow AI; Informed Intent; Final Liability rests with the Human.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack

**Order of systems in the inventory.** The inventory and risk weeks are anchored to the three stated use cases, in this order:

1. **The customer service chatbot enters first.** It is the only system stated as deployed, it is customer facing and it directly addresses the internal audit finding.
2. **AI visual inspection enters second.** It is in pilot, and your Q2 2027 objective depends on its governance being ready before production.
3. **AI sales forecasting enters third.** It is planned rather than built, so it is recorded at concept stage for early classification.

**ISO/IEC 42001 readiness.** The readiness themes in the table below describe how each week's artifacts relate to the structure of ISO/IEC 42001 (https://www.iso.org/standard/81230.html). They indicate readiness only and are not a promise of certification or audit outcomes.

| Week | Focus | Tamarack tailoring | Incumbent integration point | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | Charter drafted with the Sponsor. The Week 12 "two governed workflows" candidates are confirmed. A works council consultation trigger is defined for production staff. | Unknown | Context of the organization; leadership and roles |
| 2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot, then visual inspection, then sales forecasting. This closes the gap named in the June 2026 finding. | Unknown | Scope; AI system resources |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology | Each system is classified under the EU AI Act. Risk criteria are set. | Unknown | Planning; AI risk criteria |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments | Chatbot: GDPR, transparency and EU data residency. Visual inspection: production staff impact, quality impact and works council relevance. | Unknown | AI risk assessment; AI system impact assessment |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Operating register is populated. Treatment owners are assigned. | Unknown | AI risk treatment |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core policies are drafted and taken toward adoption. Scope decisions are made at steering. | Unknown | AI policy; leadership commitment |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle gates are set, including a pre-production gate for visual inspection. | Unknown | Operation; AI system life cycle |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection starts | Supplier review for each system. Supplier identities are Unknown. EU data residency is checked against the stated constraint. | Unknown | Third-party relationships; documented information |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight | Human oversight design for the chatbot and for visual inspection, using the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). | Unknown | Operational control; human oversight |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring metrics are defined per system. | Unknown | Performance evaluation; monitoring |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | AI incident and change paths are defined. The first evidence review takes place. | Unknown | Improvement; nonconformity and corrective action |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Readiness review against the minimum viable AIMS definition. | Unknown | Internal audit and management review readiness |

**Legal review.** Items in Weeks 1, 3, 4 and 6 with legal effect must be confirmed with external counsel. These include:

- EU AI Act classification
- GDPR assessments
- works council consultation obligations
- adopted policies

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a functioning minimum viable AIMS. It consists of six elements:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**First production workflow.** The chatbot is the only system the Profile Block states as deployed.

**Second production workflow.** Whether visual inspection will be in production use by Week 12 is `Unknown`. It depends on the program start date and the production timeline, and neither is fixed in the Profile Block. The second workflow will therefore be agreed at Week 1 so that the outcome remains achievable.

Achieving these six elements is a readiness milestone. It does not constitute certification, a favorable audit opinion or regulatory compliance.

## 5. Client Team Commitment (estimates)

The figures below are **estimates** of weekly hours per role. Each covers one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and asynchronous work between sessions. Steering weeks (1, 6 and 12) add an estimated 1.5 hours for steering participants. Which roles attend steering is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at Week 1.

| Role | Estimated hours per week | Estimated heavier weeks |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 | Weeks 1, 3, 6 and 12 |
| CISO | 3 to 5 | Weeks 4, 8 and 11 |
| Head of Quality | 3 to 5 | Weeks 5, 7 and 10 |
| Head of Data | 4 to 6 | Weeks 2, 4, 9 and 10 |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 | Weeks 4, 7 and 9 |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 2 to 3 | Weeks 2, 11 and 12 |

**Internal audit independence.** We recommend agreeing at Week 1 how the two internal auditors contribute. They should help with design and evidence quality without taking ownership of the controls they may later be asked to audit.

## 6. Steering Cadence, Logistics and Price

**Steering.** Executive steering checkpoints take place at:

- **Week 1:** mobilization and decisions needed
- **Week 6:** mid-point status and scope decisions
- **Week 12:** closing report and minimum viable AIMS attestation

**Delivery format.** Each week includes one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation.

**Dates and storage.** The program start date and session times are `Unknown` and will be scheduled after your decision. Program working materials do not require customer data. The storage location for evidence will be agreed at Week 1 in line with the stated EU data constraint.

**Price.** The price is US$60,000 for the twelve-week program. This sits within the stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Whether the program falls within that fiscal year is `Unknown`, because the fiscal year dates are not stated. Contract and payment terms have legal effect: confirm with external counsel.
